minutes.headline: Planning Board reorganized, declined to sponsor a two-family bylaw change, and continued the 150 Holmen Street stormwater hearing to June 14.
minutes.summary: The board elected a chair, vice chair and clerk and filled liaison seats, approved an ANR for 388/390 Goodrich Street, and heard a citizen's proposal to allow stacked two-family dwellings, which the members declined to sponsor. The 150 Holmen Street stormwater hearing was continued pending an ANR plan and engineering revisions. Committee reports covered open space parcels, Lake Shirley access, a possible 40B project, and the return to in-person meetings.

public_comment.topic: A phone caller identified as the owner of 388/390 Goodrich Street spoke on his ANR plan to straighten the lot line.
David Mackey responded to board concerns about his two-family bylaw proposal and the accessory unit size limit.

budget_items.what_was_said: The petitioner cited a modular builder quote for a two-bedroom home as evidence housing is out of reach.
Capital planning is done for the year with nothing to report until budget season.

budget_items.topic: State funding for lake public access
budget_items.what_was_said: A state agency reportedly has programs that would fund the improvements for public access to a water body at no cost to the town if access stays public in perpetuity.

decisions.decision: The board declined to sponsor the two-family bylaw change; Mr. Mackey may proceed by citizen petition and the board would review it before town meeting.
The 150 Holmen Street hearing continues to June 14. An ANR plan must be filed first, and revised materials are due by June 8.
The board indicated it would condition any stormwater approval on receiving the SWPPP and periodic maintenance reports.
June 14 will be the last remote meeting; in-person meetings resume June 28.
The planning director will follow up by phone on the board member who has not responded to the letter and report at the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board declined to sponsor a citizen's two-family bylaw change; the petitioner may proceed by citizen petition, with board review before town meeting.
The 150 Holmen Street stormwater hearing was continued to June 14, pending an ANR plan filing and revised materials due June 8.
The board approved an ANR for 388/390 Goodrich Street, 4-0 by roll call.
The board indicated it would condition any stormwater approval on receiving the SWPPP and periodic maintenance reports.
June 14 will be the last remote meeting; in-person meetings at town hall resume June 28.

why_it_matters: A zoning change allowing stacked two-family dwellings would now reach residents only through a citizen petition, which means a possible vote at town meeting without the board as sponsor.
The 150 Holmen Street stormwater permit is not decided, and the conditions the board signalled (maintenance reports) would govern how the site is monitored after approval.
watch_next: June 14 continued hearing on 150 Holmen Street stormwater; revised materials due June 8.
June 28 return to in-person Planning Board meetings.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the Goodrich Street ANR, the citizen-petition route for the two-family bylaw, and the four board members present. They differ on votes: the official minutes record the officer and committee nominations and a failed two-family motion, and ours records neither a result for that motion nor those elections. Ours alone records a 3-0 vote continuing the 150 Holmen Street hearing, which the official minutes do not.
